A.estimand: In future consented adult participants, 2x2 factorial effects of denominator-transparency training and leaderboard display on transfer comprehension of unseen fictional civic round records.
A.unit: person randomly assigned to arm, response to withheld fictional transfer cases
A.control: Neither rule transparency tutorial nor leaderboard
treatments: transparent explanation vs neutral equal-length tutorial
private no leaderboard vs synthetic leaderboard display
A.outcome_primary: unseen 4-item interpretation test: correct distinguish zero observed, unknown coverage, repeat agenda events, and scheduled vs attempted denominator
outcome_secondary: rate of choosing easiest 4/20 toy opportunities under fixed rewards
reported confidence calibration on same 4-item test
A.falsifier: No meaningful difference in transfer accuracy or selection, or changes explained by mismatched exposure/time, or potential harm/withdrawal.

B.H1: Denominator explanation transfers to unseen cases (not just taught labels)
B.H2: Leaderboard causes rule-dependent shortcut selection and can offset comprehension gains
B.adversary: Any gains due to tutorial answer leakage, unequal screen time, or differential attrition

C.design: Adult-only randomized 2x2 factorial, 4 arms (no leader/no transparency; transparency alone; leaderboard alone; both); all 4 get matched-duration instructions, identical fictitious events and comprehension transfer cases, conceal scoring key, document randomization before enrollment.
C.analysis: Primary difference in mean 0-4 accuracy by transparency, controlling leaderboard; separately test interaction exploratory with multiplicity; report per-arm N, missingness, attrition and uncertainty, no predictive claim from dry-run data.
C.statistical_plan: Estimate factorial ITT via OLS with transparency, leaderboard, interaction; robust SE if adequate human n, report CI not just p. Prereg power based on pilot data independent of heldout; no arbitrary invented sample size.
C.Ethics: Local institutional ethics/DPO review before recruitment; adult affirmative informed consent separately retained; no opinion/party/religion; disclose study purpose and withdrawal options; no unapproved external data transmission or participant recruitment.

papers.source: Randomized 10,000-student language app contest plus leaderboard and prizes

papers.importance: Online informed consent explicitly required even for otherwise anonymous surveys; consent records separate.

limitations: Prior studies use different outcomes/populations and gamification bundles; none establish effect on the exact PFL transfer task.
Search is targeted, not systematic review; no unique 2/3 claim.
Consent guide is institutional guidance, not legal determination for this project.

E.performed: Actual targeted online literature and ethics source inspection prior to and after prereg; no original participants or newly observed outcomes
E.output: 2x2 factorial consented human protocol with no-profiling fictional material

F: Strong alternative: familiarity with simple displayed denominator may explain success; equal-duration tutorials and holdout transfer must be blinded to teaching condition. Leaderboard may change attention rather than strategic behavior.
G: No external independent human data; future trial needed. Published examples are contextual prior art only.

H.PF_P12: Unverified cognitive benefit of fictional PFL; no support from project-specific participants
H.PF_P07: Gaming and social attention effects untested; published generic studies provide competing hypotheses
